data.reasoningText:
I confirm escapeXml fully escapes the key characters with straightforward replacement, so whatever reaches the SVG is safe even if stripHtml isn't perfect. The CodeQL alert is really flagging that regex-based HTML stripping is inherently an unreliable sanitizer pattern, not that this specific output is unsafe.

Even so, since the fix is cheap, I'll make stripHtml more robust by looping the tag-removal regex until no more changes occur, which eliminates any nested or overlapping tag bypass concerns.

data.content: Fixed. The single-pass `<[^>]+>` replace is what CodeQL flags — a nested/overlapping construction like `<<script>` can leave a live `<script>` tag after just one pass, since JS `replace(/…/g, …)` matches non-overlapping occurrences in one left-to-right scan rather than re-scanning the result. `stripHtml` now loops the tag-stripping regex until a pass removes nothing, so no residual tag can survive.
No errors. Since output also passes through `escapeXml` before being embedded in the SVG, this closes the CodeQL finding with defense in depth on both the sanitizer and the sink.
